issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` matches identifiers like `class`, `dms`, or `7s-foo`, partially defeating the fast-path
issues.detail: The pre-filter `/\dm?s/i` accepts any digit followed by optional `m` and an `s`. It will match strings like `class`, `dims`, `7something`, or hex color fragments like `#1ms...`. These false positives still enter `valueParser`, weakening the claimed speedup on real stylesheets that contain digits adjacent to s/ms in unrelated contexts.

issues.description: No stated invariant or measurement accompanies a performance change
issues.detail: The PR claims a performance fix but states no invariant for the guard ("every declaration with a time token contains a digit followed by s or ms") and provides no benchmark numbers. Knuth's rule: don't optimize without measuring. The changeset should document the before/after timing and the precise set of values the fast-path provably skips.

issues.description: Guard could be tighter and self-documenting via `\dm?s\b` plus a literate comment
issues.detail: Anchoring with a word boundary (`/\dm?s\b/i`) excludes identifier-internal matches like `dims` or `class` and better expresses intent: "a numeric literal terminated by a CSS time unit." A one-line comment naming the invariant ("any time value must contain a digit immediately preceding `s` or `ms`") would make the optimization readable rather than cryptic.

issues.description: Module-level regex is fine but `.test` on uppercase values relies on `/i` flag — worth noting
issues.detail: CSS values are commonly lowercased upstream, but `decl.value` is the raw string. The `/i` flag handles `MS`/`S`, which is correct, yet the cost of case-insensitive matching is small but non-zero. Given the hot-path framing, a brief note confirming the author considered and rejected lowercasing once would close the audit.

review.summary: The change is a sensible cheap pre-filter that short-circuits `valueParser` when the declaration value cannot contain a time token — a textbook \"avoid the expensive parse when a regex suffices\" optimization. However, the regex `/\dm?s/i` is looser than the invariant it is meant to express and will admit false positives (`class`, `dims`, `#1ms…`), partially eroding the speedup. The PR also ships a performance fix with no measurements and no stated invariant in the code or changeset, which is exactly the discipline Knuth asks for on \"perf\" changes. Tighten the regex with a word boundary, add a one-line comment naming the invariant, and include before/after numbers in the changeset. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED.
